Both earlier prints went up. Put/call open interest is 0.12, so positioning is call-heavy (baseline, sealed 2026-11-23 18:08 UTC). The stock has fallen about 14% from 19.29 (Nov 4) to 16.5-16.8. Most of that came in sympathy with peers: -5.9% on Nov 5 after Insulet's print and -8.0% on Nov 6 after Tandem's. In the last week PODD fell about 12% while MMED went from 18.65 (Nov 16) to 16.01 (Nov 20), so the run-up reads -11.5% over both 5 and 20 days. Today it bounced to about 16.76, the day Piper Sandler upgraded it to Buy with a $28 target 'after doctor calls'. Q2 revenue consensus is $825-831M: $827.5M per the Earnings Whispers / finviz preview of 2026-11-16, $825.3M Yahoo, $831.1M Benzinga. EPS consensus is $0.10-0.12. The FY27 guide is about 10.5% organic, or about $3.43B, against consensus of $3.42B. Adj. EBITDA margin is guided to about 16% and is back-half weighted after 9.9% in Q1. The previews call sentiment clearly bearish, and the debate is demand durability once the extra week is gone, plus the margin ramp. Medtronic exited its stake entirely in the Oct 14 exchange offer, which was 5.4x subscribed. Short interest fell from 20.8M to 9.8M shares between the Oct 15 and Oct 30 settlements, so the arb hedges are mostly gone.
view: This is the second standalone quarter (Aug-Oct) and the first full quarter of Flex with the Abbott-made Instinct sensor in the US, which began shipping Aug 17. It laps a weak base: Q2 FY26 Diabetes was $757M, +7.1% organic, with US orders dipping while patients waited for new sensors. On the Q1 call management said Q2 organic growth in both the US and international should look like Q1's underlying rate excluding the extra week, which is low double digits. On $757M that gives roughly $833-848M before FX. FX is about flat: the broad dollar was 0.65% weaker year on year in the quarter, but EUR was 1.8% weaker against the dollar. Consensus of about $827.5M is +9.3% reported, so it sits at or just below the low end of the company's own words. A modest revenue beat in the $5-20M range, like Q1's $843M against $828M, is the base case. Peer prints fit MiniMed taking US share. Insulet's global new starts grew only low single digits in Jul-Sep, and Insulet expects to lose a couple of points of new starts to new entrants. Tandem's US starts only just returned to growth. MiniMed's new US pumps were up more than 20% in Q1. Today's Piper upgrade after doctor calls is a dated independent trace of the same thing. The stock has de-rated about 14% into the print on peer sympathy rather than company news, so a clean beat with a reiterated or nudged-up guide should lift it, as the last two prints did. What keeps this from a recommendation: the market's line here is margin and 2027 framing as much as revenue. Tandem fell about 5.6% on a clean beat this season because of softer 2027 framing. The EBITDA ramp to 16% is steep, international CGM pricing is under pressure (Abbott cut its FY guide partly on international Diabetes pricing), and OUS 'waiting mode' ahead of the November Flex Europe launch could soften the 70%-international mix. A beat of the size I can derive is only about 1.5% of revenue, which is roughly what the last two prints delivered and the market may already expect. Net: a lean up, not a bet.
unpriced: Possibly a small gap. The stock fell about 14% on peer sympathy (Insulet new-start slowdown, Tandem's 2027 framing, tubeless entrants) while MiniMed's own data points the other way: Insulet's loss of new starts and the share gains its own pump launch implies. Consensus also sits at the low end of management's own Q2 low-double-digit organic commentary on an easy base. Neither is clearly outside the price: the commentary was public on the call, and the Piper upgrade already moved the stock about 4.7% today.

recommendation.reason: Revenue likely beats a consensus that sits at or below management's own Q2 low-double-digit organic commentary on an easy base ($757M at +7.1% organic, US weak). This is the first full quarter of Flex with Instinct, and peer prints are consistent with US share gains. But the beat I can derive is about 1.5% and is the same pattern the market has seen twice. The reaction may turn on the EBITDA margin step-up and any FY28 framing, which I cannot pin from public data. 59% is below the 65% bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q2 adj. EBITDA margin that does not step up clearly from Q1's 9.9% (around 12% or less), or international organic growth in the high single digits from waiting mode and CGM pricing, with the FY guide only reiterated. That would turn a revenue beat into a sell-the-news reaction, as with Tandem.

self_critique: The case for up is that consensus is low against management's own words, but analysts heard those words. Consensus at +9.3% reported may simply bake in an FX or waiting-mode cushion, so the 'beat' I derive may be exactly what the buy side expects, and Q1's $15M beat was the same pattern. The sector is being re-rated on 2027 competition (tubeless entrants including Tandem's, Beta Bionics), and a print that is fine on revenue but light on EBITDA could fall sharply, as Tandem did. The opposite case, for a bigger up move than I allow: a bearish, under-owned name after an index-flow split-off, two-for-two strong reactions, and a same-day upgrade on doctor checks could make a beat-and-raise a 10%+ gap.
